cands.ethicsSearched: Searched the web for House Ethics Committee and Office of Congressional Ethics/Conduct matters, STOCK Act late-disclosure reports (Insider, NOTUS/Washington Sun, Oklahoma Watch), FEC complaints or enforcement, and controversies listed on Wikipedia. No House Ethics or OCE investigation or FEC enforcement action involving Hern was found. The FEC enforcement (MUR) database and the House Ethics Committee site were not searched directly.

ethics.title: Reported apparently late stock-trade disclosures (2024–2025 trades)
ethics.summary: NOTUS reported that, based on a House Ethics Committee deadline calculator, Hern appeared to have disclosed between $4.2 million and $17.6 million in stock and corporate-security trades late. The trades ran from December 2024 into 2025, and 10 of them were 2 to 12 days past deadline; examples were a $500,001–$1 million Citigroup security sale on Dec. 3, 2024, disclosed Jan. 15, 2025, and a $250,001–$500,000 Royal Bank of Canada purchase in January 2025, disclosed Feb. 18. His office said "The filings aren't late," stating he files no later than 30 days after notification from his financial advisor and within the 45-day transaction requirement.
ethics.outcome: Disputed by Hern's office; no fine or House Ethics Committee action was reported.

sources.t: NOTUS / Washington Sun: Republican Rep. Kevin Hern Appears to Have Tardy Stock Disclosures. His Office Disputes He's Late. (Mar. 6, 2026)

record.title: Tariff Response and Damages to Exports (TRADE) Fund (H.R. 3982)
record.detail: Would let the President deposit tariff revenue collected on foreign agricultural products into a fund administered by the Secretary of Agriculture to compensate farmers hurt by lost exports, higher input costs and foreign tariffs. Referred to committee; no further action reported.

ethics.title: Late disclosure of stock trades under the STOCK Act
ethics.summary: In January 2026 Letlow disclosed more than 200 stock and bond trades after the STOCK Act's 45-day reporting deadline, some more than a year late, with total value reported in ranges of roughly $225,000 to $3.3 million. Her office said a Merrill Lynch-managed discretionary account made the trades without her direction and that she self-reported the lapse in October 2025.
ethics.outcome: The House Ethics Committee waived the $200 late-filing fee on Feb. 3, 2026; no further disciplinary action has been reported.

The Advocate
Forbes (Jan. 15, 2026)

cands.status: Republican nominee and appointed incumbent; won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary for the special election unopposed (WTOL)

cands.since: U.S. Senator from Ohio (appointed by Gov. Mike DeWine on Jan. 17, 2025 to the seat vacated by JD Vance; sworn in Jan. 21, 2025)
cands.roles: U.S. Senate (Ohio), 2025–present (appointed); Lieutenant Governor of Ohio, 2019–2025; Ohio Secretary of State, 2011–2019; Ohio Senate (6th District), 2009–2011; Ohio House of Representatives (41st District), 2001–2009; Speaker of the Ohio House, 2005–2009
cands.background: Holds bachelor's and master's degrees from the University of Dayton and worked as vice president of business and economic development at the Dayton Area Chamber of Commerce before entering the legislature.

record.title: Ratepayer Protection Act (S. 5028)
record.detail: Sponsored a bill amending the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act to set a federal standard for recovering the full, incremental costs of grid upgrades serving large-load customers such as data centers; states would have to consider adopting it. Senate Democrats blocked his Sept. 17, 2026 unanimous-consent request, and a Sept. 30, 2026 cloture vote to advance the Ratepayer Protection Act failed 57–43 (60 needed); Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called it "toothless" because states are not required to adopt the standard.

src.t: GovInfo: S. 5028 (IS) - Ratepayer Protection Act

record.title: Photo ID for voting (S. 4155)
record.detail: Sponsored a bill to require voters to present photo identification (such as a state driver's license or ID, U.S. passport, military ID or tribal ID with photo) as a condition of casting a ballot. Referred to the Rules and Administration Committee; his office said Senate Democrats blocked a unanimous-consent request to pass it.

src.t: GovInfo: S. 4155 (IS)

record.title: CHAT Act (S. 2714)
record.detail: Sponsored the Children Harmed by AI Technology Act, which would require AI chatbot operators to verify users' ages, obtain parental consent for minors, block minors from sexually explicit content, notify parents of self-harm discussions and display suicide-prevention resources, with enforcement by the FTC and state attorneys general. Referred to the Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee.

src.t: GovInfo: S. 2714 (IS) - Children Harmed by AI Technology Act

record.title: SMART OTC Act (with Sen. Maggie Hassan)
record.detail: Introduced, with Democratic Sen. Maggie Hassan, a bill to modernize the FDA process for switching prescription drugs to over-the-counter status, including directing the FDA to clarify eligible drug categories and requiring a GAO report. Husted's office announced on Nov. 14, 2025 that the bill had become law as part of an appropriations package signed by President Trump.

cands.ethicsSearched: Searched Senate Ethics Committee matters, STOCK Act and financial-disclosure issues, Ohio Ethics Commission filings, FEC enforcement, and criminal or civil cases, including the FirstEnergy/HB 6 scandal. A June 2026 Senate ethics complaint concerning a senior aide's payments from a Columbus lobbying firm was found only in partisan or unestablished outlets (Heartland Signal, tiffinohio.net) with no public disposition, so it is not listed. Senate roll-call votes were not researched, per instructions; no ICPSR number was found.

ethics.title: Ties to FirstEnergy / House Bill 6 bribery scandal (not charged)
ethics.summary: A 2020 Ohio Consumers' Counsel spreadsheet made public in April 2024 showed FirstEnergy gave $1 million in 2017 to the nonprofit Freedom Frontier with "Husted campaign" listed as the reason; his spokesperson said "The Husted campaign never received this donation and is not affiliated with any of these groups." Texts and emails from FirstEnergy executives described Husted pressing for the nuclear-plant bailout and helping install Sam Randazzo, later indicted, as PUCO chair; Husted told the Columbus Dispatch, "I was advocating for saving the two nuclear power plants." On March 11, 2026 he testified remotely in the state bribery trial of ex-FirstEnergy executives Chuck Jones and Michael Dowling.
ethics.outcome: Husted has not been charged with or accused of wrongdoing by prosecutors. The Jones–Dowling trial ended in a hung jury on March 31, 2026, and Ohio Attorney General Dave Yost said the state would retry the case.

sources.t: FactCheck.org: Ohio Democratic Ads Connect Husted to Bribery Scandal, Despite No Charges of Wrongdoing (Sept. 2026)
Ohio Capital Journal: FirstEnergy gave $1 million to boost Ohio Lt Gov Husted's campaign before scandal (Apr. 10, 2024)
News 5 Cleveland: FirstEnergy corruption case ends with hung jury

ethics.title: Undisclosed JobsOhio gifts while lieutenant governor
ethics.summary: Ohio Ethics Commission financial disclosures show Husted received gifts from JobsOhio, the state's privatized economic-development corporation, in 2021, 2022 and 2023 while he was lieutenant governor, and one from its CEO in 2024. State law requires disclosure only of the source of gifts over $75, not their nature or value, and Husted's office and JobsOhio declined to say what was given.
ethics.outcome: Disclosed as required by state law; no Ohio Ethics Commission complaint, investigation or finding has been documented.

sources.t: Ohio Capital Journal: Husted took gifts from JobsOhio while he was Ohio lieutenant governor, financial disclosures show

ethics.title: Voting-residency dispute as state senator
ethics.summary: Democratic members of the Montgomery County elections board questioned whether Husted, then a state senator, primarily lived in Kettering or in Upper Arlington (Franklin County), where his wife and children lived, citing lower utility use at the Kettering house; the board deadlocked 2–2 along party lines. Secretary of State Jennifer Brunner ruled on Sept. 21, 2009 that he was no longer a Montgomery County resident and could not vote there.
ethics.outcome: The Ohio Supreme Court granted Husted's writ on Oct. 6, 2009, holding that he was a Montgomery County resident for voting purposes and that Brunner had not followed statutory procedures.

sources.t: Ohio Supreme Court via CourtListener: State ex rel. Husted v. Brunner (Oct. 6, 2009)
Dayton Daily News: Elections board remains split on Husted's residency

cands.status: Democratic nominee; won the May 5, 2026 special-election primary over Ron Kincaid

statusSrc.t: Sherrod Brown wins Ohio Democratic U.S. Senate primary, set to face Jon Husted in November (Ohio Capital Journal, Marty Schladen, May 5, 2026)

cands.since: Former U.S. Senator from Ohio (2007–2025); founder of the Dignity of Work Institute (launched March 2025)
cands.roles: U.S. Senate (Ohio), 2007–2025 (chair, Senate Banking Committee, 2021–2025); U.S. House of Representatives (Ohio's 13th District), 1993–2007; Ohio Secretary of State, 1983–1991; Ohio House of Representatives, 1975–1982
cands.background: Holds a bachelor's degree in Russian studies from Yale and master's degrees in education and public administration from Ohio State, and wrote books including Myths of Free Trade (2006). After losing his 2024 re-election bid to Republican Bernie Moreno (50.1% to 46.5%), he was a spring 2025 visiting fellow at Harvard Kennedy School and founded the Dignity of Work Institute before announcing his 2026 campaign on Aug. 18, 2025.
cands.term: Challenging Sen. Jon Husted

record.title: Railway Safety Act of 2023 (S. 576)
record.detail: Sponsored, with Republican cosponsors J.D. Vance, Marco Rubio and Josh Hawley, a bill written after the February 2023 East Palestine, Ohio, derailment to require two-person crews on Class I trains, closer spacing of wayside bearing detectors, expanded hazardous-materials rules and higher fines. The Senate Commerce Committee approved it on May 10, 2023, but it did not reach the Senate floor.

cands.ethicsSearched: Searched Senate and House Ethics Committee matters, STOCK Act and financial-disclosure issues, FEC enforcement, and civil or criminal cases. Reports that he omitted his wife's pension from past Senate disclosures (corrected in 2023) and that his Dignity of Work PAC paid a $50,000 tax bill late in 2025 were found only in partisan or partisan-leaning outlets (Washington Free Beacon, Fox News), with no ethics-body finding, so they are not listed. The numeric DW-NOMINATE score was not available from the Voteview page, and no campaign website URL appeared in search results.

ethics.title: Late property-tax payments and duplicate owner-occupancy credit
ethics.summary: NBC News reported that Brown had paid property taxes late at least seven times on his Cleveland home since buying it in 2013, and that he claimed Ohio's owner-occupancy tax credit on both the Cleveland home and a Columbus condo, although state law allows the credit on only one property per household. His campaign manager said, "They made a mistake, have taken care of it, and paid Franklin County."
ethics.outcome: Brown repaid $616 to Franklin County, paid a $390 late penalty and dropped the credit on the Columbus condo; no formal enforcement action was reported.

items.title: Cancelling registrations of voters inactive four years (HB 1209, 1978)
items.summary: Provided that each year voter registrations would be cancelled if the person had not voted at least once in four years, and directed officials to mail affected voters a cancellation notice and a form to re-register.
items.result: Ohio House Journal records votes on June 14 and June 22, 1978; Brown voted in favor
items.areaWhy: The bill set rules for removing inactive voters from the registration rolls.

record.detail: Sponsored the Property Location Oversight and Transparency Act, amending the Agricultural Foreign Investment Disclosure Act to lower foreign-ownership reporting thresholds, require geospatial maps of foreign-owned farmland, create a public USDA data portal and flag holdings near military sites. record.title: Stop Insider Trading Act (S. 4134)
record.detail: Sponsored the Senate companion to Rep. Bryan Steil's House bill, barring members of Congress, spouses and dependent children from buying new individual stocks, requiring 7–14 days' public notice before sales and imposing penalties, while letting members keep existing holdings. A Sept. 30, 2026 cloture vote to advance it failed 53–47 (60 needed); Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called it "a permission slip for corruption, not a stock-trading ban."

record.detail: Sponsored, with Sens. Tom Cotton and Deb Fischer, a bill to impose an excise tax on investments by large private-college endowments in entities tied to foreign adversaries such as China. Referred to the Finance Committee; no further action recorded.

statements.note: He sponsored and pushed for a vote on the restriction he described; the dispute was over how far the bill goes, not whether he acted.

statements.note: His Senate bill matches his stated concern; the 2016 state law is earlier, related context on foreign agricultural investment.

said.text: "Repealing the death penalty sends the wrong message to Nebraskans who overwhelmingly support capital punishment." Statement issued with his veto.

src.t: UPI: Nebraska Gov. Pete Ricketts vetoes repeal of death penalty

did.text: As governor, vetoed LB 268, the Legislature's bill replacing the death penalty with life without parole.

src.t: UPI: Nebraska Gov. Pete Ricketts vetoes repeal of death penalty

statements.record: The Legislature overrode the veto 30–19 on May 27, 2015. Ricketts and his parents then supplied about a third of the referendum petition drive's funding (as described by the American Bar Association), voters restored capital punishment 61–39 in November 2016, and the state executed Carey Dean Moore on Aug. 14, 2018.

recordSrc.t: Death Penalty Law Remains Unsettled in Nebraska (American Bar Association, Death Penalty Representation Project, May 10, 2019)

statements.note: His veto and later funding of the referendum match his stated support for capital punishment.

cands.ethicsSearched: Searched Senate Ethics Committee matters, STOCK Act and financial-disclosure issues, FEC enforcement, and civil or criminal cases; found no ethics-body finding or enforcement action. Not listed because they involve no formal complaint or finding: criticism of his January 2023 appointment by Gov. Jim Pillen, whom the Ricketts family spent over $1.3 million helping elect (Nebraska Examiner, Jan. 12, 2023), and 2026 allegations by Osborn's campaign and the Nebraska Democratic Party that Ricketts was behind Democratic candidate William Forbes's primary run and later lawsuit, which his campaign denied. Senate roll-call votes were not researched, per instructions; note that rickettsforsenate.com is an opposition parody site, not his campaign site.

ethics.title: Lawsuit over his role in the 2016 death-penalty referendum
ethics.summary: On Dec. 4, 2017 the ACLU filed a state-court suit on behalf of Nebraska death-row inmates (Sandoval v. Ricketts) alleging that Ricketts and State Treasurer Don Stenberg violated the state constitution's separation of powers by proposing, financing, organizing and directing the 2016 referendum that restored the death penalty.
ethics.outcome: Lancaster County District Court dismissed the suit, and the Nebraska Supreme Court affirmed on Jan. 25, 2019, holding that the inmates had other remedies through postconviction proceedings; the court did not find wrongdoing by Ricketts.

sources.t: Nebraska Supreme Court: Sandoval v. Ricketts, 302 Neb. 138 (Jan. 25, 2019)
VICE: Nebraska's governor loves the death penalty so much it got him sued (Dec. 4, 2017)

cands.name: Dan Osborn
cands.status: Independent (nonpartisan petition) candidate; qualified for the November ballot after the Secretary of State verified his signatures in July 2026; no Democrat is on the ballot after nominee Cindy Burbank withdrew

statusSrc.t: Nebraska Examiner: Nebraska Secretary of State says Democrat Cindy Burbank won't appear on US Senate ballot (July 21, 2026)

cands.since: Candidate; has never held public office (former Kellogg's industrial mechanic and president of BCTGM Local 50G; 2024 independent U.S. Senate nominee)
cands.background: U.S. Navy veteran (four years, aboard the USS Constellation) who also served in the Nebraska Army National Guard, then worked from 2004 as an industrial mechanic at Kellogg's Omaha cereal plant and was president of Bakery, Confectionery, Tobacco Workers and Grain Millers Local 50G. He later worked as a steamfitter and lost the 2024 Senate race to Republican Deb Fischer, about 53% to 47%.
cands.term: Challenging Sen. Pete Ricketts

record.title: Filed independent ballot petition
record.detail: Submitted about 12,500 voter signatures (4,000 required, including 750 per congressional district) to run as a nonpartisan candidate rather than seek a party nomination; the Secretary of State verified them in July 2026. Campaign action, not an official act.

src.t: Nebraska Examiner: Dan Osborn submits signatures to challenge Ricketts on Nebraska's November ballot (June 11, 2026)

record.title: "Nebraska Fairness Plan" platform
record.detail: Released a six-point agenda pledging "No cuts to Social Security or Medicare. Ever," raising the Social Security payroll-tax cap, letting Medicaid negotiate drug prices, making no-tax-on-tips-and-overtime permanent, banning non-compete agreements, backing right-to-repair, and opposing shifting AI data-center power costs to consumers. These are campaign commitments, not official acts.

src.t: Dan Osborn campaign (Substack): My Plan to Protect Our Paychecks, Social Security, and Healthcare (Apr. 22, 2026)

record.title: Launched 2026 campaign with no-caucus pledge
record.detail: Announced a second Senate run, against Sen. Pete Ricketts, saying he would "not caucus with either party" if elected and describing himself as "unapologetically for the workers and their issues." Campaign pledge, not an official act.

src.t: Nebraska Examiner: Nebraska's Dan Osborn picks a race, launches Senate bid against U.S. Sen Pete Ricketts (July 8, 2025)

record.title: 2024 independent U.S. Senate race
record.detail: Ran as an independent against Republican Sen. Deb Fischer in 2024 and lost about 53% to 47% (Nebraska Secretary of State official canvass).

src.t: Official Report of the Board of State Canvassers, 2024 General Election (Nebraska Secretary of State)

record.title: Led Kellogg's strike as union local president
record.detail: As president of the Omaha union local, helped lead a strike by about 1,400 workers at four Kellogg's cereal plants that began Oct. 5, 2021. After Kellogg threatened to permanently replace strikers, members ratified a five-year contract on Dec. 21, 2021 with across-the-board raises and no permanent two-tier pay system. A union role, not a public office.

src.t: Kellogg strike ends as workers approve new labor agreement (Reuters via The Gazette, Dec. 21, 2021)

said.text: "I've been a registered independent from the time I could vote." Osborn said this at his 2026 campaign launch, adding that he would "not caucus with either party."

src.t: Nebraska Examiner (July 8, 2025)

did.text: Qualified for the ballot by nonpartisan petition, submitting about 12,500 signatures, instead of running in a party primary.

src.t: Nebraska Examiner (June 11, 2026)

statements.record: Voting records show he has been registered nonpartisan since at least 2004. Nebraska Democratic Party chair Jane Kleeb said "We are supporting Dan Osborn" (a party spokesman said the party does not formally endorse candidates), and the party later declined to fill its ballot line; Osborn said, "We don't coordinate with them."

recordSrc.t: Nebraska Examiner: Nebraska Dems chair 'supporting' Dan Osborn vs. U.S. Sen. Pete Ricketts (July 31, 2025)

statements.note: His registration and ballot route match his claim of independence; Democratic support came from the party's own decisions, and his no-caucus pledge cannot be tested unless he is elected.

said.text: "I'm unapologetically for the workers and their issues." Osborn said this in launching his 2026 campaign, framing the race as "the billionaire versus the mechanic."

src.t: Nebraska Examiner (July 8, 2025)

did.text: As president of BCTGM Local 50G, helped lead the 77-day 2021 Kellogg's strike, which ended with a five-year contract including raises and a path for newer workers to reach full pay.

src.t: Al Jazeera: Kellogg workers approve labour contract, ending 11-week strike (Dec. 21, 2021)

statements.note: His documented union leadership matches the worker-focused message of his campaign; he has no legislative record to compare.

cands.ethicsSearched: Searched FEC complaints and enforcement, criminal and civil cases, and other formal complaints; found the two 2026 FEC complaints listed (both filed by Republican-aligned complainants but reported by Nebraska Public Media), with no disposition. Bloomberg reported in January 2024 that Kellogg's fired him for watching Netflix at work after the strike; no grievance or legal outcome could be confirmed, so it is not listed. Reports that the campaign restructured family payments came only from Fox News syndications and were not verified.

ethics.title: FEC complaints over payments to family members and PAC spending
ethics.summary: On March 23, 2026 the conservative group Americans for Public Trust filed an FEC complaint alleging that Osborn's campaign and two PACs he is tied to (Working Class Heroes Fund and League of Labor Voters) paid his wife, other relatives and their businesses more than fair market value, including over $278,000 to his wife and her companies. In April 2026 Jeffrey Davis, chair of the Nebraska Accountability and Disclosure Commission (appointed by Ricketts as governor, filing privately), alleged the PAC's non-federal account paid about $103,000 to campaign staff in 2025 in a way that circumvented contribution limits. Osborn's campaign called the first "baseless, nuisance allegations" and said it "is fully compliant with all FEC rules."
ethics.outcome: Allegations only; no FEC finding or action had been reported as of the cited coverage.

sources.t: Nebraska Public Media: Conservative group asks for investigation into Senate candidate Dan Osborn's campaign and PACs (Mar. 24, 2026)
Nebraska Public Media: U.S. Senate candidate Dan Osborn faces another election spending complaint (Apr. 14, 2026)

ethics.title: House Ethics Committee review of office spending and an intern's pay (Office of Congressional Conduct referral)
ethics.summary: The House Ethics Committee announced in November 2025 that it was reviewing a referral about Collins and his then-chief of staff Brandon Phillips. The Office of Congressional Conduct report, released in January 2026, found "substantial reason to believe that Rep. Collins used congressional resources for unofficial or otherwise unauthorized purposes"; it alleged that the office paid Phillips's girlfriend as an intern (about $5,000 in 2023–2024, per the Georgia Recorder) while she did little or no work, and that Phillips may have spent official funds on campaign activity. The OCC said Collins did not cooperate and recommended that the committee subpoena Collins, Phillips and others. Collins's office called it a "bogus complaint"; NOTUS separately reported that Phillips was reimbursed more than $170,000 in office expenses.
ethics.outcome: Pending; the Ethics Committee extended its review, and no findings or sanctions had been reported as of September 2026. Phillips left the chief-of-staff post in December 2025 and became a senior policy adviser to Collins's campaign.

record.title: Voted for 2026-27 state budget (HB26-1410)
record.detail: Voted for the $46.8 billion Long Bill, which passed the House 43-19. To close a $1.2 billion general-fund shortfall it reduced Medicaid reimbursement rates and services by $270 million, among other cuts. Bird criticized the vote during the primary; Rutinel said he "made efforts to blunt the blow of cuts to Medicaid."

record.title: Worker Protection Act (SB25-005)
record.detail: Voted for the collective-bargaining bill, which would have made it easier to form unions by repealing parts of Colorado's modified right-to-work law (the Labor Peace Act). It passed the House on third reading 43-22, and Gov. Jared Polis vetoed it in May 2025.

src.t: Colorado General Assembly: SB25-005 House third reading roll call (May 6, 2025)

record.title: Immigration-status civil rights bill (SB25-276)
record.detail: Voted for the bill. Among other things it bars jails from delaying release for immigration enforcement, removes the affidavit requirement for in-state tuition and ID documents, and limits information-sharing with federal immigration authorities. It passed the House 42-21 and was signed May 23, 2025. His primary opponent Shannon Bird was excused for the floor vote.

src.t: FastDemocracy: SB 25-276 House roll call; Colorado General Assembly bill page

record.title: Semiautomatic firearms permit law (SB25-003)
record.detail: Voted for the bill, which from August 1, 2026 bars buying specified semiautomatic firearms unless the buyer completes a firearm safety course and gets a sheriff-issued eligibility card, and classifies rapid-fire devices as dangerous weapons. It passed the House 36-28 and became law.

src.t: Colorado General Assembly: SB25-003 House third reading roll call (Mar. 24, 2025)
